nd the body is a deterministic 10–20 character distillation of what the turn produced. Replaces the
built-in notifications row and reuses its settings namespace.
# dsh-notify-plus
English | 中文

Context-rich native notifications for **DSH Desktop** — both the official
**DeepSeek Harness** shell

(`0.2.0-rc.x`) and the earlier `DSH Desktop` shell
(`2.0.x`).

DSH Desktop's built-in notification told you that *a* turn finished. It never
told you *which* conve

rsation, or *what* the turn actually produced — so the
toast was impossible to act on:
| | Built-in | dsh-notify-plus |

| Title | `用户回合已完成` / `User Turn Completed` | `重构通知插件` — the live conversation title |
| Body | `一个由
你发起的回合已完成。` / `A user-initiated turn has finished.` | `已经修复了通知排序，现在会优先选择最近的助手…` — a distilled one-li
合已完成。` / `A user-initiated turn has finished.` | `已经修复了通知排序，现在会优先选择最近的助手…` — a distilled one-liner |

On the earlier shell the plugin replaces that built-in row and reuses its
settings namespace, so the

existing Desktop toggles keep working and no user
preference is lost. The official 0.2.0 shell remo

ved the row *and* the
notification service a plugin could call, so there the plugin raises the toast
itself. See How the replacement works.
## What it does

- **Titles every toast with the live conversation title.** The title comes from
the log-backed sessi

on title service, so it follows renames and automatic
title revisions instead of being a constant.
-

**Distils the turn into one actionable line.** For CJK replies the body is
10–20 characters; for La

tin replies it stays inside the Windows toast body
envelope. Nothing is sent to a model — the distil

lation is deterministic, so
it costs no tokens and adds no latency.
- **Keeps failure reasons.** A f

ailed turn reports the actual error instead of a
[该节后续省略]
## Requirements
| DSH Desktop | the official **DeepSeek Harness** shell — verified against `0.2.0-rc.2` — and the ea

rlier `DSH Desktop` shell — verified against `2.0.3` |
| Harness | `@deepseek-ai/dsh 0.2.0-rc.x`, an

d `0.1.1-rc.x` on the earlier shell |
| Windows | 10 or 11. The toast path uses Windows PowerShell 5

.1 and the installed DSH Desktop AUMID |
| Node | `>=22.19.0` (only for development and tests) |

The plugin depends on one harness-provided module, `@deepseek-ai/schemastery`,
which DSH already mou
nts. You do not need to install it yourself.
### A known upstream caveat

This applies to the earlier 2.0.x shell, which still ships the
`profile-preferences` record.

On those releases, edits made in **Settings → Notifications** may revert on the
next launch. The des

ktop keeps a private copy of `mode`, `openBrowser`,
`networkExposure`, and `notifications` under
`<u

serData>/profile-preferences/<profileHash>/state.json` and mirrors it back
into `settings.yaml` at s

tartup, while the settings page only writes
`settings.yaml`. This plugin reads whatever the document

says, so it inherits the
revert exactly as the built-in row does.

the report
is against 2.0.9, and the mirroring code first appears in a later release than
2.0.3.

This is deliberately **not** worked around here. That record is another
component's private source o

f truth: writing it from a plugin would add a second
writer to a single-document record that also ho

lds the user's browser and
network-exposure choices.
## Compatibility

This plugin reads harness internals that are not a stable public contract:
`sessions.on("session/eve

nt")`, `ctx.get("sessionTitle")`, the background-job
settlement stream (`jobs.onJobDone` on 0.1.x, `

jobs.events.subscribe` on 0.2.0),
and the notification surface (`desktopRuntime.notifyAttention` on

0.1.x; a
self-contained Windows toast on 0.2.0). Each of those is driven behind a
feature check and
covered by tests against the verified shapes.

Because the notification surface is now the plugin's own, a host that provides
nothing still loads:

the session observers run, the sink reports why it stayed
silent, and one broken notification never

disturbs the turn that produced it.
A release that changes the session or job shapes will stop produ

cing that kind
of notification; please open an issue with your DSH Desktop version.
### Declared compatibility

`package.json` carries a per-release declaration under
`dsh.compatibility.dshReleases`. Every entry

is either runtime-verified or
interface-verified against the published package — never assumed:
| DSH release | Basis |
| `0.2.0-rc.2` | runtime-verified: installed into a live profile on the official **DeepSeek Harness*

* shell and observed raising a correctly-shaped toast through the AUMID path |
| `0.1.1-rc.2` | runt
ime-verified: installed into a live `web` profile on DSH Desktop 2.0.3 and observed raising correctl

y-shaped toasts |
| `0.1.5-alpha.2` | interface-verified: every consumed surface has an identical si

gnature and payload shape |
| `0.1.5-rc.1` | interface-verified: same |
| `0.1.5-rc.2` | interface-v

load shape |
| `0.1.5-rc.1` | interface-verified: same |
| `0.1.5-rc.2` | interface-verified: same |

"Interface-verified" means the consumed surfaces — `sessions.on("session/event")`
with the `turn/sta

rt`, `turn/end`, `assistant/message`, and `user/message`
payloads; `sessionTitle.get(session)`; the

job settlement stream; and
`settings.register(ns, schema, options)` — were diffed against each relea

se's
published types and sources and found unchanged. It is a source-level claim, not
a runtime acce
ptance, and it is labelled as such.

`0.2.0-rc.2` additionally changed three of those surfaces, all of which are
handled here: `jobs.onJo

bDone(snapshot)` became
`jobs.events.subscribe({ owners }, listener)` delivering a `settled` event w

hose
`job` carries `status` and `label`; the namespace-scope settings API was
replaced by a `Config`

-derived form model, so the plugin exports `Config` and
keeps the legacy namespace only as a bridge;

and the native notification service
disappeared with the in-process host.

Only `win32` and the DSH Desktop host are declared. The observation layer is
platform-neutral, but t

he notification path is Windows-only, so nothing else has
been run.
